record.issuing_body: Wyoming Legislature (68th Legislature, 2026 Budget Session; sponsor Rep. Lien); signed by the Governor
record.summary: Creates crimes involving AI: distributing, promoting or threatening to distribute nonconsensual synthetic sexual material of an identifiable person (W.S. 6-4-307), and knowingly developing or distributing an AI system specifically designed to create child pornography or synthetic sexual material (6-4-308) or to promote self-harm (6-4-701), each a felony with up to ten years' imprisonment. Using AI to generate child pornography is sexual exploitation of a child. Using AI to commit a crime is no defence (6-1-206), and developers are immune from damages for misuse by others unless the system was developed knowing or intending that its primary purpose would be illegal or illicit (1-1-143).
record.notes: Passed the House 61-0 (21 Feb 2026) and, with Senate amendments, the Senate 31-0 (5 Mar 2026); the House concurred 58-1 on 6 Mar 2026. Signed by the Governor on 7 Mar 2026 and assigned Chapter 91, Session Laws of Wyoming 2026; effective 1 Jul 2026. The Act's title still refers to offences concerning the use of AI to censor political speech, but its enacted sections create no such offence. A second conviction for distributing synthetic sexual material carries up to twelve years. The development offences do not apply to systems that produce such content solely in response to user prompts without the developer's intent, to bona fide school, college, university, museum or public library activities, to law enforcement and judicial activities, or to interactive computer services for content provided by others; the self-harm offence also exempts licensed health care providers giving legitimate medical or therapeutic services.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the enrolled act for HB0102 (House Enrolled Act No. 32), stored 12 Oct 2026 from wyoleg.gov (the archiver found it unchanged on 17 Oct 2026), and the Legislative Service Office bill digest for HB0102, stored in this run from wyoleg.gov. The enrolled act confirms the title, the offences, penalties and exemptions, the developer immunity and the 1 Jul 2026 effective date (Section 3); its approval lines are blank. The digest confirms the catch title, the sponsors, the votes, the Governor's signature of HEA No. 0032 on 7 Mar 2026 and Chapter 91. The bill page stored as the secondary source is an empty JavaScript shell. The stored files do not name the Governor, so the issuing body no longer does.

changes.issuing_body: the stored files do not name the Governor; 'signed by Governor Mark Gordon' becomes 'signed by the Governor'
changes.summary: corrected: the old summary described 6-4-701 as covering AI systems that 'censor political speech'; the enacted 6-4-701 covers self-harm only (the political-speech offence survives only in the Act's title). AI-generated child pornography under 6-4-303 added
changes.notes: rewritten: votes from the digest, and the title discrepancy, the repeat-offence penalty and the exemptions from the enrolled act added; the comparison with chatbot statutes removed

judgment.status_reasoning: The digest records '3/7/2026 Governor Signed HEA No. 0032' and '3/7/2026 Assigned Chapter Number 91'; Section 3 of the enrolled act reads 'This act is effective July 1, 2026.' 1 Jul 2026 is before 18 Oct 2026, and no stored file shows a repeal. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific state criminal law on AI systems built for child sexual abuse material, synthetic sexual material and self-harm; in scope with no note (unchanged).
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's signature, 7 Mar 2026 (digest; the enrolled act leaves the approval date blank); date_in_force is 1 Jul 2026 from Section 3.
